name: Recipe Book
description: Share recipes with ingredients and step-by-step instructions, browsable by category
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may read recipes; require auth for creating, updating and deleting recipes; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
Recipes: any signed-in user may create a recipe; only its author may update or delete it (403 for anyone else); DELETE /api/recipes/:id removes the recipe permanently

Recipe validation: title is a required non-empty string of at most 255 characters; ingredients is a list of 1 to 50 non-empty strings of at most 200 characters each; instructions is a required non-empty text of at most 10000 characters; category is one of breakfast, main, dessert, snack, drink, other (default other); prep_minutes, when given, is a whole number from 1 to 1440; servings, when given, is a whole number from 1 to 100

GET /api/recipes returns active recipes, newest first, without ingredients and instructions; ?category= keeps one category, ?query= matches the title case-insensitively, ?page= and ?page_size= page the result (page_size default 20, at most 100), and total counts every matching recipe
GET /api/recipes/:id returns the full recipe, with ingredients in the order they were given
Every recipe in a response carries author, the username of the user who created it
On first start the app holds three to five sample recipes from at least two categories, authored by the admin account
Deactivated recipes (is_active false) are left out of GET /api/recipes and answer 404 on the public recipe endpoints; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-author or a non-admin, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone sees the recipe list and recipe details read-only; signed-in users also get an add button and, on their own recipes, edit and delete controls, and visitors see a 'Sign in to add recipes' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out
Recipe list: cards with title, category, prep time and author, a category dropdown and a title search box that filter the list, and previous/next paging
Recipe detail view: title, category, prep time, servings, author, the ingredients as a list and the instructions with their line breaks kept

Add and edit forms: title, category select, prep time, servings, ingredient rows that can be added and removed, and an instructions text area; show the API's validation messages next to the form, and ask for confirmation before deleting
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every recipe, active or not, with its author and category, plus total, active and inactive counts
Toggle a recipe's active status from the overview

fields.is_active: boolean (default true; false hides the recipe from public endpoints)
